blocks.etymology: From French timbre, ultimately from Ancient Greek τύμπανον (túmpanon, “drum”). Doublet of tympanum, timpani, timbal, and tymbal.

senses.definition: the special quality of a voice or musical instrument that makes it sound distinct

examples.en: The violin had a rich and warm timbre.
examples.vi: Cây đàn vĩ cầm có một âm sắc ấm áp và phong phú.

thesaurus.definition: (music) the distinctive property of a complex sound (a voice or noise or musical sound)

wiktionary.gloss: The quality of a sound independent of its pitch and volume.

examples: When someone speaks after inhaling helium, his voice has a higher timbre. With sulfur hexafluoride, the result is a lower timbre.
wiktionary.gloss: The pitch of a sound as heard by the ear, described relative to its absolute pitch.

examples: Quarterly the First quarter Siluer …, The second Siluer a Cheueron gules betweene three Castles Sables And to his timbre vpon his healme, an Elephants head in his proper Colours […]
wiktionary.gloss: The crest on a (helmet atop a) coat of arms.
